title: Start of Einer wird gewinnen with Hans-Joachim Kulenkampff on German broadcaster ARD
text: Hans-Joachim Kulenkampff, nickname Kuli was a German actor and TV host, remembered mainly as host of Einer wird gewinnen, a quiz show that ran from 1964 to 1987.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1964
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 1964 with the song "Man gewöhnt sich so schnell an das Schöne", composed by Rudi von der Dovenmühle, with lyrics by Niels Nobach, and performed by Nora Nova. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Hessischer Rundfunk, selected its entry through a national final.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1964

title: July 7 - 14th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 14th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 26 June to 7 July 1964. The Golden Bear was awarded to Dry Summer directed by Metin Erksan.

title: 27 June-5 October: documenta III
text: documenta III was the third edition of documenta, a quinquennial contemporary art exhibition. It was held between 27 June and 5 October 1964 in Kassel, West Germany.

title: 1964 West German presidential election
text: An indirect presidential election was held in West Germany on 1 July 1964. President Heinrich Lübke was renominated by the Christian Democratic Union.

title: German company Auto Union is acquired by Volkswagen Group over subsidiary Audi AG.
text: Auto Union AG was an amalgamation of four German automobile manufacturers, founded in 1932 and established in 1936 in Chemnitz, Saxony. It is the immediate predecessor of Audi as it is known today.

title: “Rote Lippen soll man küssen” by Cliff Richard
text: Lucky Lips is a song written by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller. It was originally recorded by Ruth Brown in 1956 and was successfully covered by Cliff Richard in 1963.

title: “Das kannst du mir nicht verbieten” by Bernd Spier
text: Bernd Spier was a German schlager singer and record producer. He later was a real estate broker.
listen: Das kannst du mir nicht verbieten Bernd Spier

title: “I Want to Hold Your Hand” by The Beatles
text: "I Want to Hold Your Hand" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, written by John Lennon and Paul McCartney. Recorded on 17 October 1963 and released on 29 November 1963 in the United Kingdom, it was the first Beatles record to be made using four-track recording equipment.

title: “Shake Hands” by Drafi Deutscher
text: Drafi Franz Richard Deutscher was a Sinti-German singer and songwriter.

title: “Liebeskummer lohnt sich nicht” by Siw Malmkvist
text: Siw Gunnel Margareta Malmkvist is a Swedish schlager singer and actress popular in Scandinavia and West Germany (today's Germany). She represented Sweden in the Eurovision Song Contest 1960 and West Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1969.

title: “Memphis Tennessee” by Johnny Rivers
text: "Memphis, Tennessee", sometimes shortened to "Memphis", is a song by Chuck Berry, first released in 1959. In the UK, the song charted at number 6 in 1963; at the same time Decca Records issued a cover version in the UK by Dave Berry and the Cruisers, which also became a UK Top 20 hit single.

title: “Oh, Pretty Woman” by Roy Orbison
text: "Oh, Pretty Woman" is a song recorded by Roy Orbison and written by Orbison and Bill Dees. It was released as a single in August 1964 on Monument Records and spent three weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 from September 26, 1964, making it the second and final single by Orbison (after "Running Scared") to reach number one in the United States.
